solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fare in container producing sign of overeating around fancy deck by lake

indicators.note: the belly word goes around the other pieces, wrapping the reworked deck and the lake

parts.note: a paunch, a pot belly, is the visible result of eating too much

indicators.note: by means next to, so the lake sits beside the reworked deck
fancy as a verb means to elaborate or dress up, so the letters of deck are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A dieting warning: food in a box is producing a belly, and something about a deck by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' gives CKED, and 'around' wraps the belly word round it plus L; 'Fare' is food, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is food brought from home in a box or tin, literally fare carried in a container.

clue.text: Plain advertising one found in a lot of broadcast

parts.note: PR, public relations, covers advertising and publicity

indicators.note: found in says the one is placed inside the broadcast word
a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: aired means broadcast, put out on radio or television
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Simple promotion turns up in much of what goes on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective meaning simple; it is the noun for flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open grassland, an example of a plain, especially in North America.

clue.text: Army bigwig discharging the Spanish: that illustrates it

indicators.note: discharging means letting go, so those letters are dropped from the officer

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A senior officer is dismissing the Spanish contingent, as the next part demonstrates.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the punctuation mark printed in the clue itself, between 'Spanish' and 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark printed just before these words is two dots, so the clue's own text shows an example.

clue.text: Scope in varied role around prominent part of ship getting award

indicators.note: around says the reworked role is placed round the ship part
varied means altered, so the letters of role are rearranged

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship, which sticks out
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An actor in various parts aboard ship ends up winning a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' gives ELRO, which 'around' wraps round the ship's front. OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is space to move freely, the same idea as scope meaning freedom to act.

clue.text: Bit of mischief in conspicuous place — and male is thrown out!

indicators.note: is thrown out says the letters of and and the male abbreviation are removed

parts.note: a landmark is a prominent, easily seen feature or place

explanation.surface: A prank in a public spot, and the man responsible gets ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: LANDMARK without AND and M leaves L...ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or a prank, done for amusement.

clue.text: One unwilling to support Northern queen after a year perhaps

indicators.note: after says the queen comes after the rest

parts.note: say means for example, perhaps
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A northern queen takes a year or so before she refuses to back anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A naysayer is someone who habitually objects or says no, so refuses to back a proposal.

clue.text: Familiarity shown in hotel? Not a great amount

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a bit is a small amount

explanation.surface: Guests are on friendly terms at a hotel, though only slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is something done so regularly it is second nature, closely akin to familiarity with it.

clue.text: Classical figure in Dixieland?

parts.note: Dixieland is the American South, a part of these United States; split the answer 3, 2, 2 to see it

explanation.surface: A jazz musician from the American South plays classical music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical figure' points to Greek legend, and 'Dixieland' to jazz; the hero's name split as THESE US gives where Dixieland is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero who slew the Minotaur is a classical figure, and his name split up describes the southern states.

clue.text: Judge with additional statement about lad losing head as a criminal

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of lad's synonym is dropped

parts.note: a boy is a lad
a rider is a clause added to a document or verdict

explanation.surface: A judge adds a remark in court about a young offender who has lost his composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops B from BOY to leave OY; a rider is a clause added to a statement, and 'about' just links it to the lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyrider steals a car to drive it for thrills, an offender of a particular kind.

clue.text: Free trial by taste devised when skirting a street

indicators.note: devised means worked out or contrived, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sales pitch for a free sampling session, laid on while walking past a road.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive anagram: 'skirting' means bypassing, so A and ST are left out of TRIAL BY TASTE, and 'devised' rearranges the remaining TRIALBYTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at liberty is to be free, unconfined or released from restraint; the phrase is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Punch, maybe, producing disapproving sounds, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that the word is taken by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: boos are the jeers an audience gives to show disapproval

explanation.surface: A boxer's punch draws jeers from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a blow in a fight; it is the drink, and 'maybe' marks it as one example of alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Punch is a mixed alcoholic drink, an example of the colloquial word for strong drink in general.

clue.text: Naval women's community lacking openings for celebrity

indicators.note: openings are the first letters of the two words, and lacking says those are dropped

parts.note: a Wren is a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service
a town is a community of people

explanation.surface: A naval base town where the servicewomen live is missing some ways in.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters W and T are removed from WREN and TOWN, leaving REN and OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity in the sense of fame: both mean the state of being widely known and admired.

clue.text: Stroll with number at end to get European wine

indicators.note: at end says the number letter is taken from its place and put at the finish of the word

parts.note: to saunter is to stroll

explanation.surface: Taking a walk with a numbered ticket to fetch a bottle from the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at end' takes the N of the stroll word to its finish, giving SAUTERN; 'number' looks like a count but is just N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white dessert wine from the Sauternes district of Bordeaux in France.

clue.text: Hilly area close to village? Take wrong sign by low river

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter, so only the end of village is used

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark a teacher puts by a wrong answer
to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

explanation.surface: A country walk past a village where a misplaced signpost stands beside a sluggish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is not an adjective here but the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Exmoor is an upland moor and national park in Somerset and Devon in south-west England, a region of hills.

clue.text: Trouble with two legs raised in tree

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
ON is the leg side in cricket
gam is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: An injury problem leaves someone with both legs up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket ON, the on side, is also called the leg side. The whole of AILONGAM is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering tree or shrub with large showy blooms.

clue.text: One's hired Eastern half of attractive location in posh car

parts.note: a merc is short for mercenary, a soldier who is paid to fight

indicators.note: half of means only the first half of the estate agent's phrase is kept

parts.note: des res is estate agent shorthand for a desirable residence

explanation.surface: A hired driver heads east to half of a nice spot, riding in a smart car.
explanation.walkthrough: DES RES is British estate agents' slang for a desirable residence; its first half DES is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercedes is the German luxury car brand, a byword for an expensive prestige vehicle.

clue.text: Ill-bred fellow touring SA country snubbed former PM

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rude man surrounds the country

parts.note: a churl is a rude, boorish man

indicators.note: snubbed, cut short like a snub nose, means the country loses its last letter

parts.note: Chile is a South American country

explanation.surface: A boorish man on a South American tour cold-shoulders an ex-prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' cuts off the country's tail, and 'touring' puts what remains inside the rude man word, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was Britain's wartime prime minister, so a former holder of the office.

clue.text: Pack sank at sea, part of hiker's equipment?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hiker's bag sank in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapsack is a bag carried on the back, standard gear for a walker.

clue.text: Bond in a Fleming novel eliminating fellow with time

indicators.note: with means joined to, so the time letter is attached after
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
eliminating says the letter for fellow is struck out of the fodder

explanation.surface: James Bond appears in one of Ian Fleming's books, dispatching a man against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' and 'Fleming' point at 007, but Bond is the definition, a tie. 'novel' rearranges ALEMING (A plus Fleming minus F) into LIGAMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of tissue that binds bones together, so it is literally a bond.

clue.text: Sign on set of tracks for source of loans?

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the sign sits above the tracks

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A star sign is seen on a railway line, asking where money can be borrowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loans' suggests a bank, but the question mark signals books lent out.
explanation.definitionFit: A library lends out books, so it is a place loans come from, though not of money.

clue.text: Queen with old drink getting minimal attendance

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: The monarch with an old-fashioned tipple finds hardly anyone has turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A quorum is the smallest number of members who must be present for a meeting to do business.

clue.text: Purplish colour seen in medium in Morocco

indicators.note: in says the medium word is placed inside the country code

parts.note: MA is the international code for Morocco
an agent is a medium, a means through which something acts

explanation.surface: A purple shade is spotted at a spiritualist's session in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests a psychic, but here it means an intermediary, AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red shade, a vivid crimson with blue in it.

clue.text: Source of pellets, maybe, causing small offence in Belgium and Spain

indicators.note: in says the small offence is placed inside the two country letters

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
E is the international vehicle code for Spain, from Espana
low means small, as in low numbers
the pip is British slang for annoyance or offence, as in giving someone the pip

explanation.surface: A minor diplomatic upset arising within Belgium and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives me the pip' is British slang for annoys me. The pellet source is a tube through which darts or pellets are blown.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube for shooting darts or pellets by breath, one example of something that fires them.

clue.text: Reportedly, highly desirable weight

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: a plum job is a highly desirable one

explanation.surface: Word has it that a much-coveted weight is up for grabs.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumb is the lead weight on a line used to find the vertical.

clue.text: Part of physio's outfit that is taken around clubs absolutely not new

indicators.note: taken around says the abbreviation for that is surrounds the club letter

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: not says the new letter is removed from the word for absolutely

parts.note: bang means absolutely or exactly, as in bang on time

explanation.surface: A sports physio's kit is carried round the clubs, and it is definitely not brand new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like football clubs on the physio's rounds but gives the card suit C. BANG without N is BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice bag is a pack of ice that a sports physiotherapist applies to injuries to reduce swelling.

clue.text: British composer's made-up condition

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ... was a British composer, Master of the Queen's Music
made up is British slang for delighted, so this is a state of great happiness

explanation.walkthrough: 'made-up' looks like invented; in British slang 'made up' means overjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss wrote ballet and film music, and the word also means perfect happiness.

clue.text: Congregation having fine vintage

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
vintage means old

explanation.surface: A church's members enjoy a fine old wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold is a church's flock of believers, from the image of sheep in a pen.

clue.text: Farewell from a princess with international group

parts.note: Di is Diana, Princess of Wales
the EU, European Union, is an international group of states

explanation.surface: A royal says goodbye along with a group of nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French word for goodbye, used in English as a formal farewell.

clue.text: A bachelor choosing to hide face in ban

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees

indicators.note: the face of a word is its first letter, and hiding it removes it

parts.note: volition is the act of choosing or willing

explanation.surface: An unmarried man opts to keep his face covered when there is a prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: VOLITION loses its first letter V to give OLITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Abolition is the formal ending or outlawing of something, so a ban as a noun for doing away with it.

clue.text: Sheepish expression about fly sadly close to fork in dessert

indicators.note: about says the sheep's bleat goes around the other pieces

parts.note: baa is the sound a sheep makes
a ked is a wingless parasitic fly, the sheep ked
alas is an exclamation said sadly

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of fork

explanation.surface: A timid remark about an insect landing near the fork at pudding time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' suggests embarrassment but is literal: a sheep's bleat. A ked is a sheep parasite, a wingless fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked Alaska is a pudding of sponge and ice cream encased in meringue and briefly baked.
